intro: Adán teaches organ, piano, and music theory across three institutions, and works with church musicians and student conductors in workshops and residencies.

areas.title: Organ and piano studio
areas.body: As University Organist he mentors a studio of young organists on the Borg Peterson Memorial Organ in Samuelson Chapel and teaches applied piano on the music faculty. He runs a recital series that brings international artists to the console, including the monthly Afternoon Bach Recital Series, which his students hear and play in.

areas.title: Music theory
areas.body: Theory for conservatory-track students, taught from the repertoire they play.

areas.title: Choral and orchestral direction
areas.place: Holy Family, Glendale, and the Glendale Youth Symphony
areas.body: Five ensembles at Holy Family, from the St. Cecilia Chorale to the Cherubim and Seraphim children's choirs, and the Glendale Youth Symphony, a community youth orchestra he founded and led from 2019 to 2026.

offers: Masterclasses in organ literature and service playing
University residencies combining a recital, a masterclass, and a lecture
Workshops for parish musicians on liturgy, hymnody, and choir building
Lectures on Latin American and indigenous sacred music
courses: Keyboard Harmony I, II and III
Arts and Civilization II, Honors Program
